scope: loopback only: 127.0.0.1 IPC into real lwIP, real Windows sockets, Python receiver stand-in; no radio, awdld, USB, air interface, iPhone, driver, network, channel, window or merge-parameter change
finding: tcpip_inpkt() allocates struct tcpip_msg from MEMP_NUM_TCPIP_MSG_INPKT (upstream default 8); when that pool is exhausted g_netif.input() returns ERR_MEM and the frame is dropped (counted as input_fail), so in-flight data above roughly 8 segments is lost and TCP collapses into retransmissions
change: MEMP_NUM_TCPIP_MSG_INPKT 8 -> 64 in src/awdl_netd/lwipopts.h (guarded by #ifndef), plus a soak case in tools/test_netd_tcp.py and CTest netd_proxy_soak
memory_cost: 64 * sizeof(struct tcpip_msg) (~40 B each) ~= 3 KB; measured netd working set 7.0-7.1 MB and private 2.3 MB unchanged
sweep_method: python tools/test_netd_tcp.py <netd> --case soak --mb 4 --cycles 1 --stall 0 --batch 8 [--allow-drops]; goodput = MB(10^6 B) / wall clock of the upload; 1360-byte segments; generated by build/diagnostics/Sweep-Queue.ps1 and repeated for the final binary

sweep.note: 4 MB run did not finish within the 150 s cap
16.78-26.84 MB/s across runs; the Python peer and host scheduling are the limit here

ctest.new_test: netd_proxy_soak (3 connections x 4 MB, 12 segments in flight, ~15 s)

limits: not an air-interface or iPhone result; input_fail counts rejected inbound frames of any kind (pure ACK frames too), so it is not a data-loss counter; the 8-slot default may still be sufficient at a sustained 930 frames/s and only lose frames on bursts, which remains unproven on hardware; no 24 h, concurrency or window/pool tuning was tested
